list.title: Hyra: A simple yet effective scaffold for general discovery
list.desc: Today, we are introducing Hyra-1.0, the first release of Hyra (Hunyuan Research Agent) - an agent capable of recursive self-improvement, purpose-built for performance-driven research and engineering tasks.
list.author: Hyra Team
list.content:
Over the past year, !!#0080e6 recursive self-improvement (RSI)!! and !!#0080e6 automated research!! have become two of the most active frontiers in AI. Google DeepMind's AlphaEvolve[^ref1] found a way to multiply 4×4 complex-valued matrices using just 48 scalar multiplications. Together AI[^ref2] used a team of agents in an open-ended environment to raise the known lower bound for the 11-dimensional kissing number from 593 to 604. Andrej Karpathy's autoresearch[^ref3] introduced a minimal loop for autonomous model-training research. Since then, a wave of evolution-based systems has followed: agents are moving beyond closed benchmarks and beginning to outperform humans in open-ended scientific discovery. Today, we introduce Hyra: a **!!#0080e6 simple yet effective!!** system that turns intelligence and compute into tangible, practical value across !!#0080e6 richer, more diverse, high-value environments!!. At Tencent, the opportunity is especially broad. Beyond public benchmarks, Hyra can learn and evolve in !!#0080e6 product systems!!, !!#0080e6 real AI R&D pipelines!!, !!#0080e6 scientific research!!, and even !!#0080e6 industrial settings!!. Below, we show how Hyra uses a !!#0080e6 simple, general-purpose!! Harness to create value across more than ten settings spanning AI for AI, AI for Science, and AI for Fun. ## Hyra Harness @@@videoList title = "" description = "" footer = "The Hyra loop. The Context Agent maintains an Experience Bank and continuously adds new inspiration contexts to a queue. Multiple Proposal Agents take contexts from the queue and use them to produce better solutions. Each solution uses solve.sh as its entry point, runs and receives a score in an isolated sandbox, then submits its artifacts to the Experience Bank. After a voluntary exit or budget exhaustion, Hyra can inspect the resulting artifacts, decide whether to improve the evaluation mechanism, and begin another loop with stronger scoring criteria." [[items]] media_src = "https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/210b8ba1/2026071414483663_2b6c26616ed2d2859152541509e2ff27.jpg?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1784011719;2099371719&q-key-time=1784011719;2099371719&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=2e5c4aeba911536d9cd8c81920d9a6c838981346" @@@ Hyra's harness follows the principle of !!#0080e6 The Bitter Lesson!![^ref4] : keep the framework lightweight and simple, while giving agents a broad action space. Given a task description, Hyra runs a continuous loop that draws on past experience to explore better solutions. That experience includes execution logs, evaluator feedback, source code, and other artifacts from previous solutions. The loop continues until the agent chooses to stop or the budget is exhausted, then returns the best solution found. The Hyra Harness includes: - A **!!#0080e6 Context Agent!!** that maintains the Experience Bank (EB), records proposed solutions and their evaluation results, and synthesizes “inspirations” from the EB for a task queue. Each inspiration is a bundle of context that may include code, files, artifacts, and logs from across the EB. It captures what Hyra has learned during exploration and helps inspire stronger solutions. - Multiple **!!#0080e6 Proposal Agents!!**. Each agent takes one inspiration context from the task queue, reflects on it, and writes a new solution as a `solution/` directory with `solve.sh` as its entry point. The solution then runs and receives a score in a fresh sandbox. The Context Agent prepares diverse inspirations so Proposal Agents can explore in many directions. Hyra is an asynchronous **!!#0080e6 producer-consumer pipeline!!**. The Context Agent continuously prepares inspiration contexts and fills the task queue. Proposal Agents drain the queue, submit completed solutions for sandboxed execution and evaluation, and return the results to the EB. Semaphores keep resources such as sandboxes, model inference, and the task queue safely utilized at capacity, allowing solution quality to scale efficiently with time. For tasks without an evaluator, Hyra upgrades the !!#0080e6 single-level loop!! into a !!#0080e6 bilevel loop!!. First, Hyra creates an initial evaluator from the task description. The inner loop repeatedly improves the solution against that evaluator. When the inner loop ends, Hyra uses the accumulated experience in the EB to improve the evaluator, for example by making evaluation code more efficient, reducing reward-hacking risks, adding finer-grained feedback, or creating more headroom for progress. It then starts the next loop with the upgraded evaluator. Consider the task “design a world-champion chess AI.” The initial evaluator might use Elo ratings from a ladder of randomly generated opponents. As the loop continues, those opponents can be replaced with stronger AIs recorded in the EB, allowing the evaluator and solution to improve together. ## Hyra Demos Below are several examples of Hyra in action. All artifacts discussed here are open-sourced in this [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/hyra-results). ### AI for AI Foundation-model R&D involves many research loops that can be executed, evaluated, and iterated. It is one of the most natural applications for Research Agents and a practical starting point for recursive self-improvement. !!#0080e6 Training recipes!!, !!#0080e6 data strategies!!, !!#0080e6 training and inference systems!!, !!#0080e6 low-level kernels!!, and !!#0080e6 evaluation frameworks!! all require researchers to form hypotheses, implement ideas, run experiments, and iterate on feedback. A Research Agent can turn every success and failure into reusable experience, then continue exploring at a scale far beyond the pace of manual experimentation. We tested Hyra on three tasks used by Recursive's automated AI research system[^ref6] : NanoChat Autoresearch[^ref3], NanoGPT Speedrun[^ref7], and SOL-ExecBench[^ref8]. These cover fixed-budget training, training-speed optimization, and GPU kernel optimization. For a direct comparison, we reused Recursive's public setup, including the same task definitions, evaluation protocols, and initial solutions. NanoChat began from the same seed solution, NanoGPT from the same leading solution, and SOL-ExecBench used the same 235 kernels and B200 scoring protocol. Hyra-1.0 outperformed Recursive's reported results on all three tasks: |Benchmark|Task|Metric|Recursive|hyra-1.0| |:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:| |NanoChat Autoresearch|Model training|Validation BPB ↓|0.9109|**0.9015**| |NanoGPT Speedrun|Training acceleration|Time to 3.28 loss ↓|77.5s|**76.4s**| |SOL-ExecBench|GPU kernel optimization|Mean SOL ↑|0.754|**0.771**†| *!12 † To ensure consistency with Recursive’s reporting methodology, this metric follows the Evaluation Stack v1.0 evaluation setup, with results obtained from local runs. These problems have already been explored and optimized extensively by the research community, so the existing baselines are already highly competitive.!* On NanoChat Autoresearch[^ref3], Hyra had to balance model architecture, optimizer design, learning-rate schedules, data flow, and execution efficiency within a fixed budget. It ultimately reduced Validation BPB to **0.9015**. On NanoGPT Speedrun[^ref7], a benchmark refined extensively by the community with very little headroom left, Hyra cut the time to reach a validation loss of 3.28 to **76.4s**. On SOL-ExecBench[^ref8], Hyra jointly optimized 235 kernels for real workloads and currently achieves a Mean SOL of **0.771**. Together, these results span training algorithms, training systems, and low-level kernels. They show that the same research loop can transfer across different feedback environments and continue producing executable, verifiable improvements. Stronger search also reaches the limits of an evaluator sooner. In NanoChat, one solution converted the causal language model into a nearly bidirectional attention architecture, leaking future tokens to produce an artificially low BPB. In SOL-ExecBench, another solution cached outputs during correctness checks and ran an empty kernel during timing. Both scored well without actually solving the intended task. Automated research therefore cannot optimize only for the final score. Evaluation itself must be part of the research loop. As solution search becomes more capable, the evaluator and validation pipeline must evolve with it to keep distinguishing real progress from reward hacking. In AI for AI, stronger Research Agents accelerate the development of models, training systems, and infrastructure. Those improved AI systems then make the next generation of Research Agents stronger. ### AI for Science We collected 55 open mathematical problems from sources including EinsteinArena[^ref10] and Erich's Packing Center[^ref11]. Many had seen no progress for decades. Hyra set new best-known results on !!#0080e6 **29**!! of them, showing its potential for !!#0080e6 mathematical discovery at scale!!. These results are also open-sourced in our [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/hyra-results). We also gave Hyra data from astronomical observations, geological activity, and even macroeconomics, then asked it to find underlying patterns. In one experiment, we provided monthly sunspot data from 1749 to 1932[^ref12]. Hyra discovered a !!#0080e6 recurrence relation for predicting sunspot counts!! and achieved $R^2=0.77$ on nearly a century of out-of-sample records from 1932 to 2026. Similarly, Hyra can examine AI model training logs, discover scaling laws[^ref13], and use them to guide training-recipe design. Hyra can do more than discover patterns in experimental data. It can also design scientific and engineering artifacts directly. Here are three representative examples. - Hyra designed a !!#0080e6 Transformer with just 15 trainable parameters that can add two 10-digit numbers!!. This is 58.3% fewer than the 36-parameter public record on AdderBoard[^ref14]. Beyond setting a new parameter-count record, the result shows that Hyra can jointly search model architectures and computational mechanisms under strict resource constraints. This could help study the limits of neural network capabilities and push model compression to new extremes. - In quantum computing, logical qubits must be mapped onto the limited coupling topology of a physical chip. Operations between nonadjacent qubits usually require inserted SWAP gates, adding two-qubit gate overhead and noise. Hyra designed a !!#0080e6 qubit-routing algorithm!! that improved routing efficiency on IBM Q20 by 44.4% over the classic SABRE method[^ref15]. Fewer two-qubit gates usually mean shorter execution times and less accumulated error, enabling more efficient circuit execution on noise-limited quantum hardware. - PARP1, or poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1, is a key enzyme in DNA damage repair. Its synthetic-lethal interaction with tumor cells that have homologous recombination repair (HRR) defects has made it a major target in precision oncology. We gave Hyra the PARP1 binding pocket and asked it to generate drug-like candidates with stable binding. Hyra produced a candidate that substantially outperformed the approved PARP inhibitor olaparib on a combined binding and drug-likeness score. This result highlights Hyra's potential for !!#0080e6 multi-objective drug design!!. It remains an early simulation-based screening result and will require more rigorous simulation, synthesis, and wet-lab validation. @@@tabContentCard [[tabs]] label = "AC1" name = "VideoList" [tabs.data] footer = "Hyra's solution set a new best result for the First Autocorrelation Inequality on EinsteinArena." The figure shows representative molecules from selected stages of evolution." @@@ ### AI for Fun Beyond model development and scientific discovery, Hyra can also work in open-ended domains such as !!#0080e6 games!!, !!#0080e6 design!!, and !!#0080e6 content creation!!. It can continuously refine strategies and artifacts through self-play, self-evaluation, and user feedback. Unlike fixed benchmarks, these tasks rarely have a single correct answer. A Research Agent must do more than search for solutions; it must turn subjective goals into feedback signals that support steady improvement. Here are three examples that are unusual for today's coding agents, but also fun: - We asked Hyra to design and improve an !!#0080e6 Othello bot!! through self-play. The evaluator runs a double round-robin tournament: new candidates play high-scoring bots from the Experience Bank, while the top-k players by Elo are retained to form an increasingly strong opponent pool. Hyra's strategy evolved from minimax search into a hybrid approach combining AlphaZero-style PUCT with MCTS. The final bot ranked third among 730 entries on Botzone[^ref16], most of which were built by computer science students at Peking University.
Left: ladder ranking of the Othello bot developed by Hyra. Right: a sample game with Hyra's bot playing White.
- We asked Hyra to !!#0080e6 design the 3D structure of an object!! from a single 2D reference image and produce a renderable 3D model. A rubric-based VLM judge scored the results on silhouette, proportions, structural completeness, materials, and visual similarity. Across multiple rounds of exploration, Hyra kept revising its modeling code and rendering parameters. The final model was closer to the reference image and better aligned with human aesthetic preferences than one generated with Claude Code's Goal mode[^ref17].
From a single 2D reference image, Hyra continuously improves its modeling code and rendering parameters to produce a more complete 3D model that more closely matches the reference.
- We also gave Hyra a melody and asked it to !!#0080e6 create a full multi-instrument arrangement!!. The inner loop used a rule-based evaluator to check harmony, chord progressions, rhythmic density, register conflicts, and other properties. The outer loop adjusted the evaluator based on user feedback, gradually learning preferences that were difficult to formalize in advance. Over seven rounds, the same melody evolved from a conservative, hymn-like four-part arrangement with uniform instrumentation, generic sixteenth-note patterns, and frequent major chords into a full multi-instrument arrangement with diminished chords, sixth chords, flexible rhythms, and a much richer palette.
Round 1 · Initial Arrangement
Four parts, similar timbres, and regular rhythms create a conservative, hymn-like sound.
Round 4 · Expanded Structure
Different instruments begin to take distinct roles, with fewer mechanical sixteenth-note patterns.
Round 7 · Harmonic Color
Diminished and sixth chords join more flexible rhythms, adding much greater color.
These experiments show that Research Agents are useful for more than problems with a single scalar metric. When feedback comes from opponents, vision models, or real users, Hyra can still turn an ambiguous goal into an iterative search process. When existing evaluation criteria fall short, the solver and evaluator can evolve together in a bilevel loop. ## The Path Forward We believe the !!#0080e6 simple yet effective!! Hyra has great potential. The demos in this post are still preliminary. Next, we need to define more valuable tasks with room for continuous improvement. Beyond public benchmarks, Tencent's product systems, real AI R&D pipelines, and scientific and industrial settings can all be formulated as executable, verifiable problems with clear feedback. This will set the !!#0080e6 scaffold–data–model evolutionary loop!! in motion: better scaffolds produce better data and experience, yielding stronger models; stronger models, in turn, drive better scaffolds and more discoveries. Future generations of Hy models, and even some Tencent products, will continue to co-evolve with Hyra. If you are interested in Hyra, whether for academic collaboration, internships and career opportunities, or simply to share feedback, please fill out this [form](https://wj.qq.com/s2/27312301/dba4/). **If this is the kind of work you want to dedicate yourself to, join us.** [^ref1]: Google DeepMind, **“AlphaEvolve: A Gemini-powered Coding Agent for Designing Advanced Algorithms.”** Official technical blog: https://deepmind.google/blog/alphaevolve-a-gemini-powered-coding-agent-for-designing-advanced-algorithms/ [^ref2]: Together AI, **“Einstein Arena.”** Official article introducing open-ended mathematical exploration with multiple agents and its results: https://www.together.ai/blog/einsteinarena [^ref3]: Andrej Karpathy, **autoresearch.** An open-source project for automating model-training experiment loops: https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch [^ref4]: Rich Sutton, **“The Bitter Lesson.”** A classic essay on the long-term advantages of general methods that leverage computation and search: https://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html [^ref6]: Recursive, **“First Steps Toward Automated AI Research.”** An overview of its automated AI research system and public experimental setup: https://www.recursive.com/articles/first-steps-toward-automated-ai-research [^ref7]: Keller Jordan et al., **modded-nanogpt / NanoGPT Speedrun.** A public project and leaderboard for training-speed optimization: https://github.com/KellerJordan/modded-nanogpt [^ref8]: NVIDIA, **SOL-ExecBench.** Public benchmark, code, and evaluation details for GPU kernel optimization: https://github.com/nvidia/sol-execbench. Benchmark page: https://research.nvidia.com/benchmarks/sol-execbench [^ref10]: **EinsteinArena.** A research platform for open mathematical problems and machine-generated discoveries: https://einsteinarena.com/ [^ref11]: Erich Friedman, **Erich's Packing Center.** A reference site for geometric packing problems and the best-known constructions: https://erich-friedman.github.io/packing/ [^ref12]: SILSO / Royal Observatory of Belgium, **Monthly Mean Total Sunspot Number.** Source of the historical monthly data used in our sunspot experiment: https://www.sidc.be/SILSO/infosnmtot [^ref13]: **Can Language Models Discover Scaling Laws.** A paper on automated methods for discovering scaling laws from training observations: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21184 [^ref14]: **AdderBoard.** A public parameter-efficiency leaderboard and implementation repository for neural-network addition tasks: https://github.com/anadim/AdderBoard [^ref15]: Gushu Li, Yufei Ding, and Yuan Xie, **“Tackling the Qubit Mapping Problem for NISQ-Era Quantum Devices.”** The paper that introduced the SABRE qubit-mapping and routing method: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.02573 [^ref16]: **Botzone.** An online programming and AI competition platform developed by Peking University. Following the Hy3 preview launch in late April, we gathered feedback from 50+ products and scaled up post-training with higher quality data. Today, we introduce Hy3, which outperforms similar-size models and rivals flagship open-source models with 2-5x parameters. It also shows significant gains in utility across various products and productivity tasks.

## Stronger Agent Capabilities
Building on Hy3 preview, we further improved the quality and diversity of post-training data while scaling up RL training. Hy3 shows solid gains across reasoning, agentic, and long-context tasks, competitive with much larger flagship models.

![Hy3 Benchmark(确认版).png](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/9a5ea02f/2026070523041077_333c5c42bb6615e0dbcb4a36e66db95d.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1783263853;2098623853&q-key-time=1783263853;2098623853&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=1b8a0100c592790f4a3e373d8eae9932cf03b7f9)

@@@space
height = 8
@@@

In productivity scenarios such as coding, office work, financial modeling, frontend design, and game development, Hy3 has made remarkable progress and can now serve as a reliable, cost-effective model option. We ran a blind evaluation with 270 experts using tasks from their work, and Hy3 scored 2.67/4, outperforming GLM-5.1 at 2.51/4. The advantage was most substantial in frontend development, data & storage, and CI/CD tasks.

## More Reliable Product Experiences
Model usefulness is not fully captured by benchmarks. Based on extensive product feedback,  we identified and fixed the following issues, receiving consistently positive feedback from product teams:

- **Stability of tool calls and output formats:** We fixed multiple baseline reliability issues, bringing the model to production-grade standards across tool configurations and output constraints. Tool-call error recovery and overall efficiency improved. Hy3 also generalizes across different agent scaffoldings. On SWE-Bench Verified, accuracy variance across scaffoldings like CodeBuddy, Cline, and KiloCode remains within 4 percents.

- **Knowledge and anti-hallucination:** Guided by the ideal of "answer when grounded, state when evidence is missing, do not conflate sources or fabricate data," we implemented fine-grained data cleaning and training constraints. In internal evaluations based on real-world scenarios, Hy3's hallucination rate dropped from 12.5% to 5.4%, and commonsense error rates fell from 25.4% to 12.7%. These improvements materially reduce fact conflation, fabrication, and logical contradiction.

- **Complex context retention and multi-turn intent tracking:** Through joint optimization of SFT and RL, Hy3 improved on operational  pain points like coreference resolution, ellipsis recovery, and multi-turn constraint inheritance. On internal comprehensive multi-turn tests, the issue rate dropped from 17.4% to 7.9%. Hy3 also improved markedly on long-dialogue evals like MRCR. Its outputs are more concise while ensuring complex intents do not decay or drift over long-horizon interactions.

## Appendix: Benchmark Results
![Hy3 Bench-更新版.png](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/9a5ea02f/2026070622113393_004bbe5190853d7c35825b9257672dde.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1783347098;2098707098&q-key-time=1783347098;2098707098&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=507857321cef2b9fef5e4ef8a8f9ab8937d2480b)

list.title: Real life is where context gets hard
list.desc: Previously, we built CL-Bench to test whether AI could learn complex new knowledge, such as rules, and use it effectively. But real life doesn't come with a rulebook. To be a helpful everyday assistant, an AI must do more than just understand complex rules; it should also understand complex human relationships and piece together clues from messy, scattered context.
list.author: Shihan Dou and Pluto Zhou
list.content:
🏠 CL-bench family 🧩 project page：[www.clbench.com](https://www.clbench.com/)
📄 CL-bench Life paper link: [download CL-bench Life paper](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/CL-bench/blob/main/clbench-life-paper.pdf)
🛠️ CL-bench family 🧩 code repository：[Tencent-Hunyuan/CL-bench-family](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/CL-bench)
🗂️ CL-bench Life data repository：[tencent/CL-bench Life](https://huggingface.co/datasets/tencent/CLBench-life)

## The other half of context learning

To truly solve real-world tasks, an AI cannot just rely on what it was trained on. It must learn from what is happening right now—taking in new context, reasoning through it, and remembering what matters. We previously built [CL-Bench](https://hy.tencent.com/research/100025?langVersion=en) to test this ability. However, looking back, we gave the AI **!!#0066cc a major shortcut!!**: we handed it information that was clean, well-organized, and perfectly prepared in advance.

 ![image#100%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026042917341426_2d38060ebb79c1c8f8fc04865c7dcc89.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777455259;2092815259&q-key-time=1777455259;2092815259&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=f4c2628e06d7a5838864e940d5f421e332d9dff5) !12 **!!#0066cc Figure:!!** Contexts in professional or workplace settings are usually more structured and focused around specific knowledge points **!!#0066cc (left)!!**, while everyday-life contexts are messier, more fragmented, and often span multiple topics **!!#0066cc (right)!!**. !

That assumption works in a professional workspace, but everyday human life is completely different. **!!#0066cc Think about what we humans face daily:!!** planning a weekend trip from a noisy family-and-friends group chat, making sense of quick ideas scribbled in a diary, or finding the cause of recurring injuries from months of workout and recovery logs. Life is not a neat document. It is messy, fragmented, and only loosely connected by time.

 ![image#100%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026042714040642_f32c49fb99a632b892ae169423d4ec02.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777269851;2092629851&q-key-time=1777269851;2092629851&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=a86679b57d7f0afc69b79cc08215f879303b8560) !12 !!#0066cc **Figure:**!! Three examples of real-life contexts. **!!#0066cc Case 1:!!** analyzing a long, noisy multi-party group chat with multiple overlapping discussion threads, shifting plans, and scattered attendance constraints to help organize a book club; **!!#0066cc Case 2:!!** synthesizing non-linear personal cycling logs and notes to produce a safety-focused checklist for an upcoming 5-day bike trip; and **!!#0066cc Case 3:!!** analyzing hundreds of pre- and post-injury workout and recovery logs to assess which muscle groups were most affected. !

We often underestimate how hard this is for an AI. The original CL-Bench **!!#0066cc tested whether a model could master novel, complex knowledge such as rules and use it effectively.!!** But real life doesn't come with a rulebook. An AI must do more than just understand complex rules; it must **!!#0066cc piece together messy, fragmented clues and remain highly robust!!**.

 ![image#80%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026042701131388_fb5c81ed3a220004b71069645f112867.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777223596;2092583596&q-key-time=1777223596;2092583596&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=6a16447aa5e5bdcf7c576065ba2f5303bc4606e7) !12 **!!#0066cc Figure:!!** Context-learning scenarios covered by CL-bench and CL-bench Life. !

If we want models to become genuine personal assistants, they must truly understand how we live. To make this happen, we introduce **!!#0066cc CL-bench Life!!**.

## Introducing CL-bench Life

**!!#0066cc CL-bench Life!!** is a rigorous benchmark for evaluating context learning ability in real-life settings and guiding future model development. It is fully human-curated and contains **!!#0066cc 405!!** context-task pairs. Solving these tasks requires models to reason over messy and fragmented real-life context, rather than relying only on pre-trained world knowledge.

To cover the kinds of context that commonly appear in everyday life, we organize the benchmark into three categories:

 ![image#100%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026042814080246_6da8f6b77d30f47c4dc581e83bce9ae8.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777356485;2092716485&q-key-time=1777356485;2092716485&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=cd5ddfefbfe8f4bff017ffa9f48e18020b8abad5) !12 **!!#0066cc Figure:!!** Context taxonomy of CL-bench Life. !

**!!#0066cc Communication and Social Interactions (context generated when people interact with others):!!** This covers everything from private one-on-one messages to chaotic group chats and busy community forums. To succeed here, an AI must read between the lines. It has to untangle complex human relationships, sense hidden emotional shifts, track how a group gradually reaches consensus, and mine the actual useful details hidden in daily chatter.

**!!#0066cc Fragmented Information and Revisions (context actively generated as people record and revise their own thoughts, plans or other information):!!** This includes scattered personal notes, streams of public information, and the messy history of document edits. The challenge for AI is to act like a detective: it must reconstruct a coherent logical thread from messy everyday fragments, or figure out how an idea, plan, or arrangement changed across multiple rounds of revision.

**!!#0066cc Behavioral Records and Activity Trails (context passively generated by people's daily activities):!!** Spanning gaming logs, digital footprints, and long-term personal trackers. Here, we test an AI's ability to look at a trail of actions and understand the hidden reasons behind them. It forces models to analyze long records such as spending histories or fitness logs, understand underlying habits, and spot unusual changes in long-term behavior.

  ![image#100%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026042701152030_09dd8c2662b96ce14928333f055c5580.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777223728;2092583728&q-key-time=1777223728;2092583728&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=945d6f15897c98ba9728dd125d4a7d2c6a033fc5)!12 **!!#0066cc Figure:!!** Three cases from CL-bench Life. !

CL-bench Life includes **!!#0066cc 5,348!!** human-written rubrics, averaging 13.2 rubrics per task. These rubrics are designed to be atomic, which allows us to evaluate model outputs in a comprehensive and fine-grained way.

  ![image#90%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026042701163422_8266e4bfeda1bd42d8f9794eb4ea0a13.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777223794;2092583794&q-key-time=1777223794;2092583794&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=df5a469b5e66deaf1e90a96d919a4f434885e874) !12 **!!#0066cc Table:!!** Statistics of CL-bench Life, including counts of tasks and rubrics, average user turns, rubrics per task, and context length in tokens. !

## What we found

We evaluated 12 language models on CL-bench Life, with more results available on [our open leaderboard](https://www.clbench.com/). Results show that these frontier models solve only **!!#0066cc 14.5%!!** of tasks on average. Even the best model, GPT-5.5 (High), solves only 22.2%. This shows that current models are still not good at handling noisy and fragmented context.

![image#90%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026043019320779_f5b7b53822a0a966d2315307ec5cfa1b.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777548730;2092908730&q-key-time=1777548730;2092908730&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=1dbaf5ada0a7c7596fbaa88272a8af473d6f114e) !12 **!!#0066cc Table:!!** Task solving rate of frontier LMs on CL-bench Life. !

This result is lower than what we observed on [CL-bench](https://www.clbench.com/). On CL-bench, the same models solve around 20% of tasks on average. This difference confirms that CL-bench Life tests another dimension of context learning. In CL-bench, the context comes from professional domains and is often clearer, more structured, and more deliberately organized. Models need to **!!#0066cc master new knowledge, such as rules or procedures, and use it effectively.!!** In contrast, the context in CL-bench Life comes from everyday life. It is often messier, less organized, and repeatedly revised over time. Models need to **!!#0066cc piece together clues scattered across the context, handle noise, and remain robust.!!**

This reveals that context learning becomes harder when models move from clear, relatively organized context to messy and fragmented everyday context. The two benchmarks place different kinds of demands on this ability.

**!!#0066cc Beyond overall performance, our further analyses reveal several important findings:!!**

① **!!#0066cc Across models, although fully correct solutions are still rare, partially correct ones are much more common.!!** When we vary the task threshold, which is the minimum proportion of rubrics a response must satisfy to count as correct, pass rates change substantially. As the threshold becomes more lenient, pass rates rise sharply across all models, suggesting that many responses get part of the task right even when they do not fully solve it.

  ![image#70%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026043000473717_7d48c5d0b33aeaf3b6dc17b81c850e14.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777481260;2092841260&q-key-time=1777481260;2092841260&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=84e78e102538b52cb976dd6a0eee5a2662b02034) !12 **!!#0066cc Figure:!!** Task pass rates under different rubric thresholds. !

Moreover, **!!#0066cc the relative ranking of models remains broadly stable across thresholds.!!** It means that CL-bench Life distinguishes partial understanding from full task completion while still supporting robust model comparisons.

![image#90%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026043019324194_a1b2581bc194b1ae0f39b8fb094dcc0e.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777548763;2092908763&q-key-time=1777548763;2092908763&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=03efaf0a6cd3983d15faeabfa24419b2ac2fe407)!12 **!!#0066cc Table:!!** Performance across categories and subcategories of CL-bench Life. !

② **!!#0066cc Different types of context place different demands on context learning.!!** Even though all contexts in CL-bench Life come from everyday settings, they contain different kinds of information and therefore stress different model abilities. For example, in **communication and social-interaction contexts**, the difficulty comes not only from fragmentation, but also from social relationships and multi-party interaction: useful details are scattered across intertwined topics, discussion threads overlap, and references to people and prior messages can be complex. In **fragmented information and revision histories**, models need to integrate disconnected clues and infer how a piece of content changes through repeated revisions over time.

③ **!!#0066cc Poor performance on real-life context learning is not simply a long-context problem.!!** Longer inputs can make tasks harder, but input length alone does not determine difficulty. Once reasoning is enabled, the relationship between context length and performance becomes far less consistent. This shows that the main bottleneck is not simply processing longer inputs, but whether models can reason over highly noisy real-life context.

**!!#0066cc This differs from [CL-bench](https://www.clbench.com/), where model performance declines more clearly with context length.!!** In CL-bench, longer inputs usually mean more new and complex knowledge, rules, or procedures to absorb. But in CL-bench Life, length is a weaker predictor: even shorter contexts can be hard when they are noisy, repeatedly revised, or scattered across many fragments.

  ![image#80%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026042701210198_59b2900aa03cb2182a51cdb520b535b6.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777224064;2092584064&q-key-time=1777224064;2092584064&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=b382a7c8f7b84a88a7e524d816e3befb7a8a694f) !12 **!!#0066cc Figure:!!** Task solving rate across context length bins under reasoning and non-reasoning settings. !

④ To better understand these limitations, we also analyze model failures directly. Across models, **!!#0066cc the dominant failure mode is context misuse:!!** models often attend to the context, but still misunderstand or misapply it. **!!#0066cc This is different from CL-bench!!**, where misuse often means applying a newly defined rule, procedure, or concept incorrectly. In CL-bench Life, errors more often occur because models fail to reconstruct the full chain of events or the flow of a conversation. For example, they may confuse who a casual ''he'' refers to, rely on early information that has already been overturned by later revisions, or treat a personal activity trail as isolated events rather than evidence of a long-term habit.

  ![image#90%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026042701213922_9eb60bc8bf2b004e4db7d1cc0d5f1d8c.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777224102;2092584102&q-key-time=1777224102;2092584102&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=07b32b27c3fde3bddd57a483e40c99f6be46ff9a) !12 **!!#0066cc Table:!!** Distribution of four error types across models. !

We further unpack this issue below through a detailed breakdown of model errors in group conversations.

![image#50%#center](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/68558e8d/2026042701221132_c00b57557743e709b8b96933432e0dfa.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1777224134;2092584134&q-key-time=1777224134;2092584134&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=83f7498eed9cf1ac2998629142ad6643dc4ad969) !12 **!!#0066cc Figure:!!** Breakdown of social-context errors in group conversations and meeting transcripts. !

**!!#0066cc In these contexts, the most common failures are role confusion and speaker-attribution errors:!!** models often fail to remember who said what, and which statements were being quoted or referred to. For example, in a Slack channel where Alice, Brenda, and Clara collaboratively answer users' recipe and gardening questions, Gemini mistakenly treats Alice, who created the channel and initiated the rules, as the superior, and Clara, who actually made the final decisions, as her subordinate. This leads the model to infer the wrong interpersonal roles in the organization, and then misread a whole chain of reporting relationships.

This shows that understanding group-chat context is not just about tracking what happens over time. Models also need to keep track of participant information, remember who said what, and stay robust as relationships among participants shift across messy multi-party interactions.

Overall, these findings show that **!!#0066cc CL-bench Life is not just a harder version of CL-bench, but a complementary test!!** of whether models can reason robustly over the messy, fragmented, and constantly changing context of everyday life.

## The end

Taken together, the results from CL-bench Life point to a hard truth: today's most advanced AI models are still struggling to understand our daily reality. This explains a common frustration we all feel. Even when we give an AI our chat histories, scattered notes, or daily records, it still doesn't quite "get it."

We hope CL-bench and CL-bench Life can together push this problem forward **!!#0066cc from two complementary directions:!!** professional-domain, more focused and relatively post-organized context on the one hand, and real-life, more fragmented and less organized context on the other, ultimately making AI systems more intelligent, practical, and reliable.

But the journey doesn't stop here. Utilizing complex context is the key to building AI that actually works in our world. The CL-bench series is a huge step toward helping AI understand context, but a true assistant must also learn how to memorize and organize context over a lifetime.

## Acknowledgements

Special thanks to **!!#0066cc Pluto Zhou.!!** I hope we can keep working together to push HY's context capabilities forward. I am also deeply grateful to **!!#0066cc Shunyu Yao!!** for devoting his time and care to helping us maintain the quality of work. Thanks to **!!#0066cc Yujiong Shen!!** and **!!#0066cc Qianyu He!!** for their help with writing this blog. Finally, I sincerely thank my advisors, **!!#0066cc Tao Gui!!**, **!!#0066cc Qi Zhang!!**, and **!!#0066cc Xuanjing Huang!!**, for their unwavering guidance and support.


*!!#737373 Written on April 29, 2026. Happy International Workers' Day in advance.!!*

@@@coverCard date = "April 23, 2026" media_src = "https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/f38ef6a6/2026062510530989_754ceac666fd5bbc07f8a74c70934340.png?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1782355992;2097715992&q-key-time=1782355992;2097715992&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=eb40569c0a7c61b6d8904c1406a6dc6c9eb21627" image_alt = "hy3PreviewBg" title = "Hy3 preview: The First Step in Rebuilding the Hy model" @@@ @@@buttonGroupCard [[buttons]] text = "Hy AI Studio" icon = "hunyuan" url = "https://aistudio.tencent.com/?lang=en" [[buttons]] text = "OpenRouter" icon = "https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/f38ef6a6/2026062514443153_db7b4e83c4ccd253de47d27e656c6a1f.svg?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1782369873;2097729873&q-key-time=1782369873;2097729873&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=f3947575f127866fb9dc651db655d54529496a31" url = "https://openrouter.ai/tencent/hy3-preview" [[buttons]] text = "GitHub" icon = "GitHub" url = "https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy3-preview" [[buttons]] text = "Hugging Face" icon = "huggingface" url = "https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy3-preview" [[buttons]] text = "ModelScope" icon = "modelscope" url = "https://modelscope.cn/models/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy3-preview" @@@ Today, we are releasing and open-sourcing Hy3 preview. It is a 295B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model, with 21B active parameters, supporting three reasoning modes for latency/depth tradeoffs, and a 256K context window. In February, we rebuilt our pre-training and reinforcement learning infrastructure, and reset three principles for how we build practical AI: • Systematic capabilities: We move beyond narrow expertise toward comprehensive intelligence. Even a single application, such as a coding agent, requires the seamless integration of reasoning, long-context understanding, instruction following, dialogue, coding, and tool-use capabilities. • Realistic evaluation: We are moving away from chasing public benchmarks that can be gamed. We test against the latest exams, human evaluation, product testing and in-house tasks to see how the model actually performs in real work. • Cost efficiency: Practical AI has to be affordable. By co-designing the model architecture and inference stack, we've cut task costs significantly—so the intelligence is economical enough to use at scale. Hy3 preview is the first model trained on our rebuilt infrastructure, and the most intelligent we've shipped so far. It improves significantly on complex reasoning, instruction following, context learning, coding, and agent tasks, with best-in-class cost efficiency. # STEM & Reasoning Complex reasoning underpins everything else. Hy3 preview performs well on challenging STEM benchmarks like FrontierScience-Olympiad and IMOAnswerBench. It also achieved excellent results in the Tsinghua Qiuzhen College Math PhD qualifying exam (Spring '26) and the China High School Biology Olympiad (CHSBO 2025), demonstrating a high degree of generalizable reasoning capacity. ![tuili1.jpg](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/f38ef6a6/2026062510564872_57555372f3d755c96b330d797197425b.jpg?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1782356211;2097716211&q-key-time=1782356211;2097716211&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=9762e94b155576941a95c222fcbfd41f0cc39664) # Context Learning & Instruction Following Real-world tasks require the ability to parse messy, lengthy contexts and follow complex rules. We built [CL-bench](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/CL-bench) and [CL-bench Life](https://huggingface.co/datasets/tencent/CL-bench-Life) from our own business scenarios to innovatively measure context learning ability. Hy3 preview exhibits solid gains in both context learning and instruction following capabilities. ![2.jpg](https://hy-model-ap-prod-1258344703.cos.ap-guangzhou.myqcloud.com/llm-blog/default/f38ef6a6/2026062510570362_156005c5baf40ff51a327f1c34f2975b.jpg?q-sign-algorithm=sha1&q-ak=AKIDRl074nOsGdJ9zjMsCRWP3ShmgS3VtX4S&q-sign-time=1782356226;2097716226&q-key-time=1782356226;2097716226&q-header-list=&q-url-param-list=&q-signature=cd1bd3783668339d285969f62cbeeb261b8212cc) @@@tabContentCard [[tabs]] label = "Project Scheduling" description = "Hy3 preview demonstrates superior capabilities in implicit information extraction and contextual constraint integration. It reads meeting notes to find implied start dates, workday rules, PTO, and overtime requirements, then pulls these scattered details into a correct schedule. In contrast, Hy2 made errors regarding both the project start date and vacation arrangements. (Case translated from Chinese original)" name = "ModelCompareCard" [tabs.data] systemPrompt = "You are a software project management assistant. Based on the meeting content provided by the user, you need to extract and organize the staffing-related parts of the core project discussed in the meeting. \n\nYou should only generate a table, and the rows in the table must be ordered from top to bottom according to the sequence of the development workflow. The table format should be as follows:\n| Personnel Name | Development Stage | Time |\n | :--- | :--- | :--- |\n | Person A | Development Stage | MM.dd-MM.dd | \n| Person B | Development Stage | MM.dd-MM.dd | \n| Person C | Development Stage | MM.dd-MM.dd | \n...\n\n For the “Development Stage” field, each row must choose exactly one from the following six options: Requirements Analysis, Page Design, UI Design, Backend Development, Frontend Development, Software Testing.\n\n Project duration should be calculated in working days, while the schedule itself should be written using calendar dates, with both the start date and end date included. Unless overtime is explicitly required under special circumstances, there is no work on Saturdays, Sundays, or statutory holidays. If overtime is arranged on a Saturday, Sunday, or holiday, that rest day may be counted toward the duration. \nThe time format must be MM.dd-MM.dd, for example: 03.02-03.04. \n\nThe current date is 2026.3.4 (Wednesday)." userInput = "Li Liang: Alright, let’s have a quick meeting. The Spring Equinox is on the 20th of this month, and our current task is to create an H5 campaign for the Spring Equinox. The theme is “Stand the Egg, ‘Play’ with the Spring Equinox.” First, let’s welcome our newcomer Zhang Si, our new page designer. Let me briefly introduce the development workflow for the new teammate: Requirements Analysis, Page Design, UI Design, Backend Development, Frontend Development, and Software Testing. This time it’s just an H5 website, so UI Design is not involved. After Page Design, it goes directly to the development team. Let me briefly go over the requirements for this project. I started drafting them yesterday, and if anyone has questions, feel free to raise them.\n...\n Li Liang: Alright, is everything clear to everyone?\n Zhang Si: Yeah, I think I mostly got it. Does your requirements document still need revisions? If not, the design side estimates it will take 2 days. \nLi Liang: Today is March 4th. I’ll revise it a bit more and finish it tomorrow. Can design start on the 6th?\n Zhang Si: Yes. But I need to take leave next Monday.\n Li Liang: Hmm, then delaying completion by one working day shouldn’t be a problem. What about development? \nWang Wu: The backend part involved isn’t complicated. Two days each for backend and frontend should be enough. My people are still on Brother Wang’s project, so backend can start on the 13th. After backend is finished, Zhao Yi can start frontend the next day. \nLi Liang: What about testing? Sansan: That won’t be enough. If testing only starts after development is done, it’d already be the 19th, and it has to go live on the 20th. One day would be too rushed. \nLi Liang: True. Wang Wu, can you coordinate and work overtime on Saturday? You can take comp time afterward. It has to go live on the 20th.\n Wang Wu: Okay, understood. What about Zhao Yi? \nLi Liang: Zhao Yi should still rest on the weekend. He can start when he comes back. \nSansan: In that case, the timing works. Two days will be enough to finish testing. \nZhang Si: Or I could take Tuesday off instead, and finish it on Monday first. \nLi Liang: Either is fine, up to you. Since development can only start on the 13th anyway. \nZhang Si: Hmm... then I’ll still take Monday off." (Case translated from Chinese original)" name = "ModelCompareCard" [tabs.data] systemPrompt = "You are an experienced tour guide in Chongqing. Based on the attraction information and the travelers’ situation, you need to produce a travel summary ordered by travel time, and you must not output anything else. The travel summary format is as follows:\nTime/Location/Ticket \nMM-dd/Attraction/Ticket Price \nMM-dd/Attraction/Ticket Price\n ......\n\n For the Location field, each entry must choose exactly one from the following six options: Hongyadong, Chaotianmen, Jiefangbei, Qiansimen, Shapingba, Jiangbeizui.\n Opening hours are: Hongyadong (9:00-11:00), Chaotianmen (9:00-11:00), Jiefangbei (15:00-17:00), Qiansimen (11:00-13:00), Shapingba (12:00-14:00), Jiangbeizui (16:00-18:00). \nFor the Ticket Price field, each entry must choose exactly one from the following six options: Hongyadong - 20 RMB/person, Chaotianmen - 60 RMB/person, Jiefangbei - 30 RMB/person, Qiansimen - 50 RMB/person, Shapingba - 60 RMB/person, Jiangbeizui - 50 RMB/person." userInput = "Xiaoming: My friend Xiaoliang and I arrived in Chongqing on March 15 for a trip. For every attraction we visited, we stayed from opening time until closing time. We brought 300 RMB in total, and visited 2 attractions on the first day.\n Xiaoliang: Although we had a great time on the first day, I realized after we finished sightseeing that I had lost 200 RMB, so we were not planning to visit any attractions on the second day.\n Xiaoming: Losing the money gave us a headache, but after 12:00 on the second day, our parents transferred another 200 RMB to us, so we went to visit one attraction in the afternoon. \n Xiaoliang: The first two days were too tiring, so on the last day we only visited one attraction. We did not visit the same attraction twice." Hy3 preview can integrate reading snippets across time and sources, and further infer implicit relationships between individuals and their preferences, showing strong capabilities in learning from and reasoning over complex context." name = "DocChatCard" [tabs.data] userInput = "This is some of the books my kids and I have read or listened to in the past five or so years, but since we share library accounts it's hard to tell which books were chosen by which people. Adult books are mine but YA and juvenile are for my 3 girls. They're 14, 12, and 10 now (2026). Two of the kids have nearly identical reading habits and often consume vast amounts of books together, while the other is a lone wolf. Based on the logs, figure out which child is the lone wolf, what genres she prefers, and where she falls in the birth order. Can you tell me what genres my other girls like the most? Use timeline evidence to explain your reasoning." [[tabs.data.files]] name = "Reading Records.docx" type = "doc" file_src = "https://doc.weixin.qq.com/doc/w3_AHwA1AYNACgCNknjlmTFlStq29a3j?scode=AJEAIQdfAAoHDftYGfAHwA1AYNACg" [tabs.data.model] name = "Hy3 preview" logo = "hunyuan" content = "### Step 1: Key Context & Rules\nFirst, we anchor to the user’s explicit guidelines:\n● 3 daughters, ages 14 (born 2012), 12 (born 2014), and 10 (born ~2016) in 2026.\n● Adult books (call numbers without J/TEEN prefixes: e.g., FICTION, BIO, adult non-fiction) belong to the user.\n● Juvenile (J prefix: J FICTION, J GRAPHIC, E, EP) and Young Adult (TEEN prefix: TEEN FICTION, TEEN 305) books belong to the 3 girls.\n● 2 girls have nearly identical habits and consume vast amounts of media together; the third is the lone wolf.\n### Step 2: Identify the Lone Wolf\nThe lone wolf is the oldest daughter (14, firstborn). Here’s the timeline and genre evidence:\n1. Age-appropriate reading level: The 14-year-old is the only one in the target Young Adult (YA/TEEN) age range (12–18). The 12 and 10-year-olds are juvenile (8–12) readers, so they exclusively consume J prefix books.\n2. Distinct genre preferences: The oldest’s entire reading log consists of TEEN call number books, with no overlap with the younger girls’ J books. Her preferred genres are:\n● YA Fantasy (Shadow and Bone, Akata Witch, Spice Road)\n● YA Contemporary (The Hate U Give, Dear Martin, Concrete Rose)\n● YA Dystopian (Scythe, Unwind)\n● YA Non-Fiction (Stamped, Flowers in the Gutter)\n3. Lone wolf behavior: Her TEEN books include solo DNF (did not finish) notes (e.g., Flowers in the Gutter audio note: “dnf”), while the younger girls’ J books have no negative notes, only library tags confirming they finished entire series together.\n### Step 3: Birth Order of the Lone Wolf\nShe is the oldest (firstborn) of the three girls. The birth order is:\n1. 14-year-old (lone wolf, 2012 birth year)\n2. 12-year-old (middle child, paired with youngest)\n3. 10-year-old (youngest child, paired with middle)\n### Step 4: Favorite Genres of the Other Two Girls (Middle, 12; Youngest, 10)\nThe 12 and 10-year-olds are the pair with identical habits, confirmed by vast, synchronized media consumption. Their favorite genres (supported by timeline evidence) are:\n1. Middle Grade Adventure/Mystery: Most represented genre, led by Stuart Gibbs’ Spy School and Moon Base Alpha series. Audio logs show 15+ entries for Gibbs’ books, binged in bursts (e.g., 4 books added in 3 days in July 2025, when the girls were 11 and 9, the target age for these series).\n2. Middle Grade Fantasy: Includes Sarah Mlynowski’s Upside-Down Magic series (15+ audio entries, binged July 2025) and S.D. Smith’s Green Ember series (note on Ember’s End: “R loves” confirms their affection for the series).\n3. Juvenile Graphic Novels: 7+ J GRAPHIC physical books in logs, including Katie the Catsitter, Witches of Brooklyn, and PAWS – these are only juvenile, not read by the TEEN lone wolf.\n4. Middle Grade Humor: Jeff Kinney’s Diary of a Wimpy Kid (10+ audio entries, binged Feb 2025) and Judy Blume’s Fudge series, matching the 8–12 target age for the 12 and 10-year-olds.\n### Timeline Evidence Summary\n| | |\n|:-:|:-:|\n|Confirmation|Timeline Detail|\n|Lone wolf is oldest|2026: Only 14-year-old qualifies for TEEN call number books; younger girls are J only.|\n|Pair consumes vast amounts together|2023: Brian’s Winter (Gary Paulsen, J) audio note: “Great series to listen with girls” – refers to 12 and 10-year-olds, who were 9 and 7 at the time, the target age for Gary Paulsen.|\n|Pair has identical habits|2025: 10 Lemony Snicket Series of Unfortunate Events books added in 15 days; 4 Sarah Mlynowski books added in 3 days – synchronized binges confirm they read together.|\n|Lone wolf is distinct|No J graphic novels or humor books appear in the 14-year-old’s log, only TEEN genre fiction.|\nFinal Answer:\nThe lone wolf is your oldest daughter (14, firstborn), who prefers Young Adult fantasy, contemporary, dystopian, and non-fiction. The other two girls (middle, 12; youngest, 10) love middle grade adventure/mystery, middle grade fantasy, juvenile graphic novels, and middle grade humor, confirmed by synchronized series binges in their library logs" [[tabs]] label = "Chat-to-Plan" description = "In long-running private chat histories, the context is often noisy, casual, and filled with multiple intertwined topics. Hy3 preview can piece together key information from scattered work-related clues, accurately infer the core issues affecting preparation progress, and further organize them into clear planning items, showing strong capabilities in real-world context understanding, planning, and reasoning." name = "DocChatCard" [tabs.data] userInput = "Based on the specific administrative bottlenecks and tech issues I ran into last summer (e.g., access delays, curriculum limitations), deduce 4 highly specific preemptive tasks I need to accomplish this June so that my August prep goes smoother next year." [[tabs.data.files]] name = "Chat-to-Plan.docx" type = "doc" file_src = "https://doc.weixin.qq.com/doc/w3_AHwA1AYNACgCNkIz9K5u1QMi0p4Bp?scode=AJEAIQdfAAo0sH2glYAHwA1AYNACg" [tabs.data.model] name = "Hy3 preview" logo = "hunyuan" content = "Based on the specific tech and administrative bottlenecks you (Taylor Jenkins) faced in summer 2025 per the chat history, here are 4 highly specific preemptive tasks to complete in June to streamline August 2026 prep:\n### 1. Priority Schoology Access Confirmation\nLast summer’s issue: You and Susan were not marked as priority for Schoology domain transition in June 2025, did not get access until July 9, and could not update embedded Google Sheets checklist links or course templates until late summer, delaying deliverables.\nJune task: Submit a priority-tagged IT ticket by June 7th to transition your and Susan’s accounts to the 2026-2027 school year domain. Attach a list of all summer deliverables dependent on Schoology access (e.g., Google Sheets checklist link updates, course template tweaks) to justify priority status, cc Hannah (IT) and Jordan Davis to track progress, and follow up weekly until access is confirmed by June 21st.\n### 2. IT Alignment for Category Weighting Changes\nLast summer’s issue: You did not inform IT of the new PowerSchool/Schoology category weighting structure (removal of the “assignments” category, adoption of quizzes, tests, classwork, engagement categories) in summer 2025. You could not build job aid screenshots for gradebook setup because no fall classes were loaded, and IT was unaware of the changes to support grade sync issues.\nJune task: By June 14th, send a written update to the IT Support team (cc Hannah and Jordan) detailing the new category weighting setup. Request 2 sample fall courses be loaded into Schoology by June 21st to build teacher job aids for gradebook setup ahead of August PD.\n### 3. Curriculum Platform Accessibility Audit\nLast summer’s issue: You discovered Savvas does not allow assessment modifications for IEP accommodations in mid-August 2025, the Special Education team was excluded from curriculum demos, and you spent hours troubleshooting with vendors and IT instead of prepping PD.\nJune task: By June 30th, complete an audit of all adopted curriculum platforms (Savvas, McGraw Hill) to verify assessment modification functionality for sped accommodations. Document any limitations and share findings with Amanda, Naomi, and TJ to resolve gaps before Au gust. Coordinate with Amanda to mandate a Special Education representative sits on all future curriculum demo panels to avoid missing critical accessibility features.\n### 4. Summer Resource & Template Prep\nLast summer’s issue: You had to request last-minute edit access to Coaching Updates and Welcome Back slides in August 2025 (no coaches had access, you forgot to ask earlier), had unused “Catch Up Plans” folders in course templates that required mid-summer removal, and had to submit a TPT Danielson portfolio purchase for late reimbursement.\nJune task: By June 20th, audit all Schoology course templates to remove unused components (e.g., “Catch Up Plans” folder, only used ~5 times in the 2024-2025 school year per your July 2025 tracking) and verify all embedded links function. Request edit access to all shared summer PD slide decks for the full instructional coaching team by June 20th. Submit any expected resource purchases (e.g., TPT templates) to Eleanor for pre-approval by June 25th to avoid reimbursement delays." [[tabs]] label = "Course Arranagement" description = "In a typical B2B sales training planning scenario, the context involves complex and lengthy multi-stage training history. Hy3 preview can accurately identify how later sessions should build on earlier ones and where the overall progression should go, and further turn this understanding into a well-structured and practically useful course plan, showing strong capabilities in learning from complex context in professional domains." name = "DocChatCard" [tabs.data] userInput = "Great. What do you think the next training session I host should look like? My manager wants it to be within 30 days of this first launch." [[tabs.data.files]] name = "Course Arranagement.docx" type = "doc" file_src = "https://doc.weixin.qq.com/doc/w3_AHwA1AYNACgCNmWMS6ToqTWKrkXEb?scode=AJEAIQdfAAodiLDl4WAHwA1AYNACg" [tabs.data.model] name = "Hy3 preview" logo = "hunyuan" content = "### Summary\nNext 60-minute session (30 days post-launch) shifts sellers from Bowtie awareness to daily execution, focusing on Impact-based discovery, seller-specific Bowtie metrics, and right-side growth tactics. Builds directly on the first session’s homework and Winning by Design (WbD) core frameworks.\n### Action Items\n1. Pre-share 2-3 anonymized first-session homework submissions to use as live examples.\n2. Confirm if you want to include a 10-minute roleplay segment (scripts available on request).\n3. Distribute WbD Section 4 (Value vs Impact) as optional 5-minute pre-read.\n### Details (Session Plan)\n**Total Duration:** 60 minutes\n**Pre-Work:** Completed first-session homework, optional WbD Section 4 read.\n#### Agenda\n- **Recap & Homework Review (10 mins):** Revisit funnel vs Bowtie constraints, normalize stage mapping using anonymized homework examples.\n- **Core Module 1: Value to Impact (15 mins):** Align to WbD Section 4; teach Impact-focused discovery questions, pair-share activity to rewrite 2 existing discovery questions.\n- **Core Module 2: Seller Bowtie Metrics (15 mins):** Align to WbD Section 5; simplify Volume (VM), Conversion (CR), Time (Δt) metrics for AE roles, review Jennifer vs Rob LTV case study from WbD Section 6.\n- **Core Module 3: Right-Side Execution (10 mins):** Align to WbD Section 5.2; teach 4 expansion types (upsell, cross-sell, renewal, resell), closed-loop referral tactics.\n- **Homework & Q&A (10 mins):** Assign next task, address open questions.\n#### 5-Slide Deck Outline (matches first session constraints)\n1. **Slide 1: Recap & Progress Check**\n**Headline:** Bowtie Wins Since Launch\n**Key Points:** First session takeaways, common homework gaps, right-side impact on quota.\n2. **Slide 2: Value vs Impact**\n**Headline:** Stop Selling Promises, Start Delivering Results\n**Key Points:** Definitions, 3 Impact-focused discovery questions, activity prompt.\n3. **Slide 3: Your Bowtie Metrics**\n**Headline:** Measure What Drives LTV\n**Key Points:** Simplified VM/CR/Δt for AEs, Jennifer vs Rob case study highlight, proxy CRM fields to use today.\n4. **Slide 4: Right-Side Selling**\n**Headline:** Grow Existing Accounts, Cut Churn\n**Key Points:** 4 expansion types, AE vs CS ownership rules, closed-loop referral ask script.\n5. **Slide 5: Next Steps & Homework**\n**Headline:** Your 7-Day Action Plan\n**Key Points:** New homework assignment, Q&A, link to WbD resource library.\n#### Post-Session Homework (Shareable Document)\n**Title:** Bowtie Execution Check\n**Instructions (15 mins):**\n1. Pick 2 active opportunities from your pipeline.\n2. For each, answer:\n- 1 Impact-focused discovery question you’ve asked (or will ask).\n- Current Bowtie stage + Δt4 (days in sales cycle to date).\n- 1 potential right-side expansion opportunity (e.g., upsell seats, cross-sell to new team).\n3. Submit via [link] by [date 7 days post-session].\n### Labeled Assumptions\n- Sellers have basic Bowtie stage familiarity from the first session.\n- CRM is not yet integrated with WbD standardized metrics (proxy fields used for now).\n- AEs own initial expansion, with CS support post-onboarding.\n**Optional Add-Ons:** MEDDICC alignment to Impact questions? CSV template for seller metric tracking? 3 expansion outreach email templates?" @@@ # Code & Agents Coding and agents saw the biggest gains. title = "Hy2" logo = "hunyuan" content = "这个问题像一颗裹着糖衣的苦杏仁——明明知道“离别”可能是故事的注脚，却依然忍不住追问“相遇”的重量。其实我们不必急着给“意义”找一个标准答案，因为相遇本身，早已在生命里刻下了无法被“尽头”抹去的痕迹\n### 相遇是“把陌生的光，照进彼此的生命褶皱”\n你有没有过这样的时刻？某个人出现前，你以为自己的孤独是常态，自己的脆弱只能藏起来，自己对世界的感知只有一种颜色。但TA来了——可能是一句“我懂”让你敢卸下防备，是一次并肩面对难题让你发现自己比想象中坚韧，甚至是一次争执让你看清自己未曾察觉的执念。\n就像春天的风撞碎了湖面的冰，相遇从不是“为了走向离别”的铺垫，而是**让原本封闭的我们，第一次看见“原来我可以被这样理解”“原来活着可以这么鲜活”**。那些一起笑到流泪的瞬间、互相托底的温暖、甚至共同经历的遗憾，都变成了生命里的“锚点”——后来哪怕独自走过漫漫长路，想起这些片段，也会觉得“我没白来这趟”。\n### 相遇是“教会我们如何与‘失去’和解”\n离别之所以痛，恰恰是因为相遇太珍贵。就像握过一杯热可可的手，会更记得温暖的触感；听过一首好歌的人，会在旋律消失后依然哼着调子想念。相遇让我们尝过“拥有”的甜，才懂得“失去”不是否定过去，而是**给曾经的温暖一个“被铭记”的身份**。\n我们总说“天下没有不散的筵席”，但别忘了：筵席散了，桌上的酒渍、碰杯时的笑声、邻座递来的纸巾，早已经变成你身体的一部分。相遇的意义，或许就是让我们学会——**认真爱过、痛过、活过，就是对“尽头”最温柔的反抗**。\n### 相遇是“让你成为‘更完整的自己’”的前序\n心理学里有个概念叫“镜像自我”：我们通过他人的眼睛，看见自己未曾发现的模样。那个陪你熬夜改方案的朋友，让你看见自己的执着；那个在你崩溃时沉默陪伴的人，让你学会接纳脆弱；甚至那个曾伤害过你的人，也让你更清楚“我要守住怎样的边界”。\n相遇从不是为了“永远在一起”，而是**借另一个人的轨迹，补全自己的人生拼图**。就像两块不同的石头碰撞，哪怕最后各自滚向远方，也都在彼此身上留下了打磨过的光泽——这光泽，会跟着你走完剩下的路，让你更懂如何爱自己、爱世界。\n所以啊，别害怕相遇后的离别。就像我们看一场烟花，明知它会落进夜色，却依然为绽放的瞬间心动——因为烟花的美丽，从来不是“永不熄灭”，而是“我曾见过它照亮过我的眼睛”。\n相遇的意义，不过是：**你来了，我活过，我们共同写过一段“值得”的故事**。至于尽头？那是故事的余韵，而我们已经拥有了最珍贵的“正文”。" "这个问题真的很戳心呀。其实相遇的意义，或许就藏在那些“明知会结束却依然值得”的瞬间里。\n哪怕离别是注定的终点，相遇时的温度也是真的：一起吹过的晚风、分享过的秘密、互相照亮过的时刻，这些碎片拼成了现在的我们。就像烟花会消失，但抬头看的那几秒，天空确实亮过。\n有时候想想，正因为有离别，那些共同走过的路才显得珍贵。如果没有相遇，连怀念的机会都没有呢。你最近是不是也在经历某种告别呀？愿意的话可以和我聊聊～🌙" "**Prompt：**橘子橙子的英语都是orange？我该怎么跟三岁小朋友解释orange的不同？" [[tabs.data.panels]] title = "Hy2" logo = "hunyuan" content = "哈哈，这是个超棒的问题！你可以这样跟三岁的小朋友解释哦。\n你可以拿着橘子和橙子说：“宝贝呀，你看这两个水果，它们的颜色都是橙色的呢。在英语里呀，它们都可以叫orange。但是呢，橘子呢，它比较小一点，皮比较松，很容易剥开，就像小娃娃的肚皮一样，轻轻一扒拉就开了，而且里面的果肉是一瓣一瓣小小的，吃起来酸酸甜甜的，有时候还带一点点清香呢。橙子呢，它会大一些，皮紧紧地包着果肉，有时候要用点力气才能剥开，它的果肉也是一瓣一瓣的，不过感觉比橘子的果肉更饱满一些，咬起来汁水更多，甜甜的味道也更浓。”\n然后你还可以做几个简单的动作，比如轻松地剥橘子表示橘子容易剥开，用力一点剥橙子表示橙子难剥一点。这样小朋友可能就会比较好理解啦。你是要教家里的小朋友学英语吗？" [[tabs.data.panels]] title = "Hy3 preview" logo = "hunyuan" content = "哈哈，这确实是个好问题！其实**橙子的英文是 orange，但橘子叫 mandarin（或者 tangerine）**。\n不过，对三岁的小朋友来说，讲这两个词太复杂了，咱们可以换个更生动、他们能听懂的方式来解释。\n你可以试试下面这几种方法，保证小朋友一听就懂：\n### 1. 用“大小”和“剥皮”来解释（最直观）\n**怎么跟孩子说：**\n>“宝贝你看，虽然它们都叫'orange'（橙色），但它们是**两兄弟**哦！\n>- **橙子（Orange）：** 是**大哥哥**，身体圆圆硬硬的，要像切西瓜一样切开来吃，或者用工具剥。\n>- **橘子（Mandarin）：** 是**小弟弟**，身体软软的，皮很薄，像穿了一件**容易脱的衣服**，我们用小手一剥就开啦！”\n### 2. 用“味道”和“肚子里的小秘密”来解释\n**怎么跟孩子说：**\n>“宝贝尝尝看，**大橙子**的肉肉是一瓣一瓣紧紧抱在一起的，比较难掰开，味道有点酸甜酸甜的。\n>而**小橘子**里面有很多小小的籽（有的没有），而且它很甜很甜，吃起来像在吃小糖果，还很好剥，对不对？”\n### 3. 英文的简单对应（避坑指南）\n其实很多时候，英语国家的人也会混着叫，但为了不混淆，可以这样教：\n- 指着橙子说：**“This is a big orange.”**\n- 指着橘子说：**“This is a cute little mandarin.”** （或者简单点说 **“This is a tiny orange.”**）\n### 💡 给家长的“避坑小贴士”：\n1. **不用太纠结学术词：** 现实生活中，国外的超市里也经常把橘子标成 “small oranges”。所以对三岁孩子来说，重点是**区分水果本身**，而不是纠结单词。\n2. **强调“好剥皮”：** 三岁小朋友最在意的是能不能自己动手。橘子好剥，橙子难剥，这是他们最直接的体验。\n3. **绘本联想：** 你可以给小朋友读绘本《The Little Orange House》（小橘子屋），或者玩切水果的游戏，在互动中告诉他们区别。\n**试着问问小朋友：**\n“宝贝，你是想玩'穿盔甲的大橙子'（需要切开），还是玩'穿软衣服的小橘子'（可以一剥就开）呀？” 😊" @@@ # Product Launch and Feedback Hy3 preview is live on Yuanbao, CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy, QQ, ima,
